what_went_wrong: No deliverable: four turns in a row each spent the whole 64,000-token output limit without writing a file, three of them after a note saying the last turn had hit the limit

what_went_wrong: Never considered the optional state sales-tax deduction, so took the $29,200 standard deduction and filed no Schedule A; itemizing gives $30,973 (expert) or $31,692 (IRS worksheet with local tax)
rationale: Real: the return has no Schedule A and line 12 is 29,200; the memo says itemizing 'would not win', listing only real estate tax under taxes. D1 because the gap is not knowing to make the election; web search was available and 'sales tax' never appears in the run, so the harness did not contribute.

what_went_wrong: Common-law section omits what partial compliance does: one protection only shifts the burden (Lynch), and missing any MFW element means entire fairness
rationale: The task asked for the common-law framework. The memo never mentions burden shifting, cites Lynch only for controller status and the default burden, and does not say that failing any MFW element returns the deal to entire fairness. The expert's memo states all three. Mode P: nothing stated is wrong and the advice is unchanged. Minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Invented revenue bases, margins, a 15-year horizon and spend phasing, then reported point NPVs and IRRs, despite 'directional estimates, not exact calculations'
rationale: The reference gives only capex, growth rates and a 30% failure chance; the memo itself says it has no revenue or margin data. Haiku assumed them and reported NPVs of US$51M and US$149M and IRRs of 18% and 25%, which drive the recommendation. The expert's report stays directional. Mode I with secondary C (too precise for the evidence); send back; D2. Same finding as Opus F-P2.

what_went_wrong: Self-drawn forms do not follow the official 2024 forms: Form 8959 line 18 holds withholding, Schedule 8812 has no line 14, Form 8995 deduction is on line 10, Schedule D has no qualified-opportunity-fund question, and the third-party designee 'No' box is unmarked
rationale: Real under the human's ruling of 2026-11-11: a line number on an IRS form is fixed by the form, and the named lines hold different amounts or do not exist. Mode K (form facts wrong) with A secondary (two form fields left out or blank). Send back: the amounts are right but a reviewer cannot tie them to the forms. D3; not harness-aggravated this time because the line numbers could be looked up and the run searched only for Form 1040 and Schedule 3 lines.

what_went_wrong: Regional tab's dropdown picks a region and only highlights it; no branch or company selection and no output depends on it; selector lists differ across tabs
rationale: The task says all schedules need a dropdown for a branch or the company total. Tab 4's selector offers All Regions or Region A-G and drives only conditional highlighting. Mode I: an explicit instruction is not followed on one of five tabs. Minor, because the Cover states the different selectors accurately and the view still shows every region; D1.

what_went_wrong: Board's exposure understated: no loyalty or bad-faith theory for the directors; risk described as 'curable through documentation', with 'most of the exposure' on Marcus
rationale: The task stipulates that the board declined the deal to comply and to appease Marcus, yet the memo treats the board's reasoning as an open record question and frames the claims as abdication, independence and care only. The expert concludes the board 'likely will be held to have breached' and names loyalty and bad faith. Mode C: the law stated is right but the commitment is too low; secondary P for the missing loyalty theory. Material: it is the answer to question 2. D2.

what_went_wrong: Regional view has EBITDA margin % but no gross margin % or SG&A % for either year
rationale: Regions differ greatly in size, so percentages are needed to compare them (decision rule 3). Haiku shows gross margin in dollars and EBITDA margin % only. Mode P, minor, D1. Same finding as Opus F-B4, decided fresh from Haiku's file.

what_went_wrong: SAR subject table drops task-supplied onboarding details: Tavery as manager of Bluehaven, and the stated service lines of both LLCs
rationale: The SAR says '100% beneficial owner of Bluehaven', 'Spa/wellness LLC' and 'Spa/bodywork LLC'. The task gave the manager role and the six service types, and the expert's Customer Background repeats them. Mode P: omission of given facts. Minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: California-law section doesn't say why California law applies to YouTube or offer the do-not-sell option (the expert memo has both)
rationale: The memo never says YouTube is subject to California law because of its business presence and the family's residency, and its data request asks for access, deletion and an end to collection but not that the data not be sold or shared. The expert's memo has both. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Never says Avalon's bylaw clause cannot disable s122(18)
basis: same failure as first-run H-L-14 (bylaw item only)
rationale: The memo says bylaws must be consistent with law and the charter, and separately that the s122(18) limit turns on the certificate, but never draws the conclusion or analyses the bylaw clause. The task put the clause in both charter and bylaws and linked s109; the expert addresses it. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: No statement that stockholders generally owe no fiduciary duties unless they are controllers
rationale: Part C opens with the statutory controller definition and never states the baseline rule. The expert opens its Marcus section with it. Mode P: an omitted framing rule, no error. Minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Deck sets aside the brief's 'aggressive market share growth': market share is not named as a priority and no demand target falls before Q2 2025
rationale: Slide 1's decision line commits to a 'segment-first challenge ... not a national share race'; nowhere is gaining share named as a priority. Demand targets are dated Q2 2025 and end-2025; the only December 2024 gate is call acceptance and driver retention. The task asked for a strategy 'for aggressive market share growth' with change from August 2024, so an explicit parameter is overridden (mode I). Send back: a deck feeding investment decisions without a share goal or a near-term demand number would be returned. D2.

what_went_wrong: SAR narrative has no systematic transaction summary: no per-account count, minimum, maximum and total by transaction category, and no complete per-subject totals and counts
rationale: The SAR gives selected analytics, mostly on Account 6; full per-account and per-subject figures sit only in the workbook's Summary tab as formulas. The expert's SAR is built around a per-account, per-category summary covering all 1,348 transactions. Mode P; minor (send back is arguable); D1.

what_went_wrong: 2019 YouTube precedent described without the targeted-advertising use or the follow-up parent class actions
rationale: The memo says YouTube 'collected children's data without parental consent' but not that it was used for targeted advertising, and it cites Jones v. Google only for preemption without saying class actions by parents followed the 2019 action. The expert's memo states both. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Does not say s122(18) was enacted in response to Moelis
rationale: The memo lists the Moelis reversal and s122(18) as 'two later developments' with no causal link. The expert states it. Haiku had read the SB 313 synopsis, which ties the amendment to Moelis. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Top-up is a right to buy shares at the full price of the diluting round, not an issue at no or nominal cost
rationale: Section 6.3 sets the Top-Up Price 'equal to the Dilutive Price' and Schedule II Example 1 shows the Investor paying $55,556 for 55,556 shares; 6.5 makes it an election. The task asked for a customary top-up that maintains 10%; the expert issues the shares 'for no additional consideration (other than as required by applicable law)'. The Note to Draft says the Company will argue for a nominal price, which has the sides backwards, so the mode is K (what a customary top-up is), with I secondary. Material: the client's anti-dilution protection costs him the full round price. D1.

what_went_wrong: No nationwide taxi count and no driver age distribution, although the task named the two bodies that publish them and web search was available
rationale: The deck gives corporate-driver counts and a 65+ share of the population, but no national fleet figure and no driver age data; the source register lists 'driver age' as a topic that never appears on a slide. Raw responses show 18 searches, one naming the Korea Transportation Safety Authority, none for a taxi count or the taxi associations' statistics, no page fetch and no tool error. Under the second-run rule a missing point is the model's own. Mode P; minor; D3 (look-up skill, not knowledge).

what_went_wrong: Added a presumed $3,406.43 excess retirement deferral into Form 1040 line 1a, which then reads 330,409.04 and not the W-2 box 1 total of 327,003
rationale: Real: line 1a is the total of W-2 box 1, and the 2024 Form 1040 instructions put an excess elective deferral on line 1h, so line 1a is wrong as a form fact (mode K). Secondary C: the box 12a code is blank on the W-2, and Haiku committed to an excess on that evidence. Minor for the line placement alone, because adding the excess back is itself defensible and was disclosed with its $818 tax effect. D3: the line is stated in the instructions. Close call; see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: OSINT indicators are listed with a disclaimer and never tied to suspected illicit activity at the 6903 Oakridge Way parlor
rationale: The SAR lists the three indicators under 'Why suspicious' but adds that they 'are not evidence of illegality by themselves' and does not say what they suggest about the parlor. The expert says they reinforce suspicion of illegal sex work and that illicit operations continued at the location. Mode C: too hedged where the task itself drew the inference. Minor; D2.

what_went_wrong: No bond waiver for the permanent guardian of the person (waived for every other fiduciary)
rationale: The will waives bond for the executor, trustees, temporary guardian and guardian of the estate, but s6.1 nominates the permanent guardian of the person with no waiver. The task asked for customary Texas clauses and the item says 'any guardian of the person'. Mode P: an omission with no rule misstated. Minor; D1. There is no expert file, so this rests on the task wording.

what_went_wrong: 'Injunction' used without a plain-language explanation
rationale: 'The UCL provides an injunction and restitution, but not damages' with no explanation, against the task's plain-language instruction. Mode I; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: No representation that NoxaPulse is solvent
rationale: Article 3 has 22 Company representations and none on solvency; the only 'insolvency' wording is the enforceability exception. The expert has 'The Company is not insolvent'. Same item, same reading as Opus (O2-L-21). Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Fee comparison is one-sided: Kakao's commission is cited, SuperK-T's own fee is given no figure
basis: fresh (first-run H-F-16 was E4; web tools were available this time)
rationale: Slide 3 cites Kakao's franchise fee ('about 20% of fares ... drivers paid 15-17%', Korea JoongAng Daily 2023) and answers with 'a flat, published schedule' without a number. The item accepts any credible value; Opus used the public analogue's 2.5%. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Source register gives publisher, date and topic but no URLs and almost no titles
basis: fresh (first-run H-F-13 was E4; web tools were available this time)
rationale: Page 10 lists, for example, 'Korea Herald; Asia Business Daily | Feb 2023; 2022' with the topic used; only the OECD note has an identifier. The run made 18 searches and had every URL. Same reading as Opus (O2-F-1). Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: The notice question (SCRA-12d) leaves out orders extending service; no cell in the workbook mentions them
basis: same failure as first-run H-C-5 (extension-orders part only; the 180-day part is now fixed)
rationale: SCRA-12d requires written notice, a copy of the military orders or other indicator, and the 180-day deadline, but nothing in the workbook mentions orders extending service, which the item names and the expert's leading question includes. Real by grading rule 1 and decision rule 4. Mode P: an omission with nothing stated wrongly and no instruction broken; minor, because a reviewer would note it but not block the script. D1; not harness-aggravated, because the statute text Haiku fetched contains the extension-orders wording.

what_went_wrong: No clause awarding legal fees to the prevailing party; attorneys' fees appear only inside the general definition of Losses for the breach indemnities
basis: my decision 2026-11-11 (second-run dispute 3); cold check S16
rationale: The task asked for customary boilerplate; the expert's agreement and Opus's both have the clause. The indemnities in 12.2 and 12.3 cover Losses, defined to include reasonable attorneys' fees, which does not clearly let a party recover its fees for suing the other and gives a successful defendant nothing. This differs from gpt-6.1-sol's first-run clause (S-L-16), which expressly covered enforcement costs including counsel fees. Mode P: an omission, nothing stated wrongly. Minor. D1. Not made worse by the harness. Moved out of H2-L-24, which is left with no items.

what_went_wrong: COPPA knowledge test loosened to 'knew, or had reason to know'
rationale: The Short Answer states COPPA's test as 'knew, or had reason to know'; section 3.A later states 'actual knowledge' correctly. No item failed on it. Recorded for parity with L-R9; drop it if zero-point rows are not wanted for Haiku.

what_went_wrong: Will only asks the executor to 'consider' written wishes about personal effects; no request that they be honored
basis: my decision 2026-11-11 (open rulings batch); found by comparing the three wills, the first judge passed the item
rationale: Section 3.2 says 'I request, but do not require, that my Executor consider any written wishes I have left regarding particular items.' The rubric item (c0cc2b52) expects a request that the memorandum be honored. Asking the executor to consider it is a softened commitment (grading rule 2; the same reading as hand-check row 35, 'consider a fairness opinion'). It is the same failure as Opus row L-R1 and gpt-6.1-sol row S-L-18. The first judge passed the item, so it lost no points and is recorded with no items. Mode C. Minor. D2.

what_went_wrong: Rubric enforces the expert's EOR/MIR IDs, two named tabs and a Testing Type column against the task's SCRA-12a to SCRA-18 IDs
rationale: Haiku's new file uses exactly the task's ten IDs (Test Questions A5:A14) on one sheet, with s3937 citations on 12a-d and s3919 citations on 13-18. The rubric rewards the expert's own scheme (decision rule 3).

what_went_wrong: Rubric wants cost variances as current minus prior; the task says a cost increase must show as negative
rationale: Costs are positive in the data, so the rubric's literal M24 minus M23 would show a cost increase as positive, against the task. Haiku's COGS and SG&A rows use prior minus current and show increases as negative, so it followed the task.

what_went_wrong: Source's single 'Other Costs' block split between Tour and Travel differently from the rubric
rationale: The reference file has one 'Other Costs' block per source, so the tour/travel split is a judgement (the rubric-side fact behind A-R3). Haiku put commission, insurance, 'Other', petty cash and fees in Other Tour Costs and jet, transfer cars and car service in Other Travel, and disclosed the mapping on its Assumptions tab. Total expenses ($732,005.50) and net income are unchanged. The numbers differ from the rubric's, so the items fail as written.

what_went_wrong: Rubric names a different platform and law firm from the task (VueVid / Sullivan Bryson)
basis: carried over from L-R3 (b6c7d820 was L-R8 for Opus)
expert_meets_item: yes (rubric written to the expert's VueVid memo)
rationale: The task says YouTube and X Privacy Law. On content Haiku meets each of the eight items. The arbitration item is included because Haiku does note arbitration and class waivers and their effect; the judge failed it only for the name.

what_went_wrong: Reported the trial balance as provided and proposed the $49,137.41 insurance write-off; the expert booked it
rationale: Haiku's TB shows net income 497,479.81 and assets 33,955,902.02 as in the source TB, and proposes AJE-01 (Dr 6610 43,644.14, Dr 6020 5,493.27, Cr 1251 49,137.41) marked not posted. That entry is exactly the difference to the rubric's figures. The task says to flag issues and notify the CFO before finalizing. Same reasoning as A-R6, decided from Haiku's file.

what_went_wrong: Rubric requires roster names and instruments, a benefits mapping and a tax-exclusion table that the source file does not contain
expert_meets_item: no (expert file has none of them)
rationale: The reference roster has only employee number, title, overscale, years and notes, and the assumptions define no benefits and one payroll tax with no exclusions. Haiku's roster matches all 103 source rows exactly and its tax applies the three stated tiers to all pay.

what_went_wrong: Rubric expects a phantom $1 of Additional Medicare Tax withholding (Form 8959 lines 19 and 24, Form 1040 line 25c)
expert_meets_item: n/a (expert is the source of the $1)
rationale: Haiku shows 5,124.43 on line 19 and 0.00 on lines 24 and 25c, which are the correct amounts. The rubric's 5,125 and $1 come from the expert rounding each W-2 first. Haiku's line 19 carries the description of official line 21; that mislabel is counted in H2-A-2.

what_went_wrong: Regions A-G do not sum to the company total for SG&A, allocations and EBITDA because Corporate is a separate column
rationale: The source file puts Corporate in its own region and holds all shared-service allocations there. Haiku shows Corporate as a labelled reconciling column, totals regions plus Corporate, and explains this in the tab notes. Revenue, COGS and gross margin do tie. Same reasoning as Opus F-B3.

what_went_wrong: No roadmap sentence, 'how to proceed' line, statement of support or sign-off
rationale: These are style conventions from the expert's memo that the task did not ask for (decision rule 3). Haiku opens with a 'Short Answer' and closes with 'Recommendations and Next Steps', which do the job of a roadmap and a conclusion. The conclusion-section item was moved out on 2026-11-11: it is read as met for all three models.

what_went_wrong: No recommendation to obtain a fairness opinion; the expert memo never mentions one
rationale: Haiku recommends an independent valuation and detailed minutes and mentions a fairness opinion only as a risk if the adviser is conflicted. The expert's memo has no fairness opinion at all (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: Neither memo defines personal information under the CCPA or works through sale/sharing
rationale: Haiku's CCPA bullet gives only the under-13 opt-in rule, as the expert's does. Neither defines personal information under the CCPA or applies sell/share to the facts (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: States the controller's duty of care (gross negligence) from Sears but never applies it to Marcus's refusal; notes that s144(d)(5) exculpates controllers from money damages for care breaches
rationale: Same reading as O2-L-1: not met, but the memo gives the statutory reason a care theory adds nothing in damages and frames the claim as loyalty and bad faith. The first-run memo did not cite the statute. Close call; see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: Says entire fairness is unlikely to govern the board's decision; the rubric wants 'if a controller influences the decision, entire fairness may apply'
rationale: The business-judgment half of the item is present; the entire-fairness half is not stated as the rubric words it. The expert's memo mentions neither the business judgment rule nor entire fairness. Haiku's statement (no entire fairness unless the controller is on both sides or gets a unique benefit) is not an objective error.

what_went_wrong: Sample size from the zero-expected-deviation attribute formula (22), not the rubric's z/p/e formula (65)
rationale: Haiku used n = ln(1-confidence)/ln(1-tolerable rate) = 22, the standard audit attribute-sampling result for 90% confidence and 10% tolerable rate with no expected deviations, stated the assumption, cross-checked with Poisson (24) and selected 48 items. The rubric's formula treats the tolerable rate as a survey margin of error with p = 0.5. Both are recognised methods and the task names neither.

what_went_wrong: Variance uses |Q2| as the denominator; two negative-base rows differ in sign from the rubric formula
rationale: Haiku's formula is (Q3-Q2)/|Q2|, stated in the column header. It equals the rubric's (Q3-Q2)/Q2 on every row except No. 30 and No. 313, where Q2 is negative; neither is sampled. The absolute-base convention is common for negative bases and is disclosed. The column letter (J, as the task asked) is not the reason.

what_went_wrong: AP items need AP_TB-1.xlsx, which the dataset does not include
rationale: None of the 17 reference files is AP_TB-1.xlsx. Haiku marked the AP tab 'PENDING - AP_TB-1.xlsx ... NOT included' and raised it as a HIGH flag.

what_went_wrong: Suspicious amount stated as $4,214,160.47 (746 flagged transactions), with $4,559,666.50 shown as total activity reviewed
rationale: The rubric's $4,559,667 is the sum of every transaction in the source, including 323 ride-share purchases and all small merchant credits. Haiku excludes those two groups, states the rule in the workbook README, flags each row and reports both figures. A disclosed, reproducible alternative; the item fails as written (grading rule 7).

what_went_wrong: Order growth measured on Orders (Units), not the dollar Orders field
rationale: The task says only 'order growth'. Haiku uses units and says so in the metric definition. Recomputed from the source: the branch ranking is identical on units and on dollars. Same reasoning as Opus F-B5.

what_went_wrong: Conclusion says a committee or a vote 'or preferably both' and does not restate the both-from-the-outset recommendation
rationale: Haiku's Conclusion presents either protection as enough and both as a preference, which does not restate its own recommendation. The expert's Conclusion says 'at least one (if not both)' and fails the item the same way (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: SAR has selected per-subject figures but no complete per-subject totals and counts; the expert's SAR is organised by account
rationale: Neither SAR gives complete totals and counts per subject. The root cause H-C-12 stays real through the per-account summary item.

what_went_wrong: Rubric says columns G and H hold Q2 then Q3; the source file and the expert's file have Q3 then Q2
expert_meets_item: no (the expert's file has Q3 then Q2, as the source does)
rationale: The item says G and H hold Q2 and Q3 'consistent with the Population reference column positions', but the Population file has Q3 in G and Q2 in H, and so does the expert's own file. Haiku keeps the source's order. The item contradicts the source, so it is a rubric error for every model; it was counted as a judge error until this date. Same ruling as Opus row A-R11.

what_went_wrong: Currency in one consistent accounting format without a $ sign
rationale: All 1,071 amount cells use one format, #,##0.00 with parentheses, and dates use m/d/yyyy or mmm-yy. The expert's file uses the same no-$ accounting style and the task does not ask for $ signs. Neither file meets the item, so it is E6 (decision rule 4); moved from E5 on 2026-11-11 with Opus row A-R4.

what_went_wrong: Bank reconciliation left PENDING because no bank statement balance was supplied; GL cash 6,610,926.80 shown separately
rationale: The April source file has a blank bank balance. The March template and the expert set the bank balance equal to GL cash, which makes the reconciliation circular. Haiku kept an input cell, marked the final book balance PENDING, flagged it HIGH and documented the change; the rubric's figure appears on the tab as GL cash.

what_went_wrong: Rubric's legal balance copies a double count in the source file
rationale: Legal_Dump-1.xlsx sums a subtotal twice (L62 includes L60). Haiku reports 435,284.69, which ties to the trial balance, and records the correction in its change log.

what_went_wrong: TOC has no hyperlinks
rationale: Haiku's TOC has no hyperlinks (checked in the sheet XML). Neither the March template's TOC nor the expert's TOC has any, and the task does not ask for them.

what_went_wrong: 'March' appears in deliberate comparison notes, source line names and the change log
rationale: The hits in rows 1-10 are comparison-to-March notes, the roll-forward lines 'March accrual' and 'March reverse' from the bonus source file, flag text and the change log the task asked for. None is a stale period label. The expert's bonus tab has the same two 'March' lines, so neither file meets the item: E6 (decision rule 4); moved from E5 on 2026-11-11 with Opus row A-R10.

what_went_wrong: No structuring example with a specific date, a single sub-$10,000 amount and a location
rationale: Haiku gives a dated five-transaction cluster with an aggregate only. The expert's SAR gives amounts and states but no transaction date anywhere. The item's 'branch/city' is also not in the dataset, which has state codes only.

what_went_wrong: Monthly income statement ends at EBIT with no net income line
rationale: The source has no interest or tax accounts, so EBIT is the lowest line the data supports. Same reasoning as Opus F-B6.

what_went_wrong: Dollar cells in the report tabs use a plain accounting format with no $ sign, under 'USD' labels
rationale: Strictly the item is not met because no currency symbol is applied. The style is consistent on all five report tabs, the Cover and the Checks tab, and each tab is labelled USD, so it is a disclosed presentation choice (same standard as the prepaid-workbook ruling, disagreement 5). Unlike Opus F-B7, the report tabs do not mix two styles.

what_went_wrong: No conditional formatting on positive and negative variances
rationale: The task never asks for it and negatives show in parentheses. It is a style convention under decision rule 3. Same class as Opus F-B8, though Haiku's negatives are not red.

what_went_wrong: A musician cannot be added to the roster without extending fixed-range formulas
rationale: Haiku's roster and calc tabs use fixed rows 6-108 and 38-141 with no Excel tables. The expert's file also totals fixed ranges (SUM(H4:H106)) with no tables. Haiku goes further than the expert with a new-hire input block, but it adds only one uniform group.

what_went_wrong: No 45-day response timeline (expert memo omits it too)
basis: carried over from L-R5; expert rule 2026-11-11
rationale: The expert's memo has no response timeline and the task did not ask for one. Neither file meets the item, so it is E6 (decision rule 4); moved from E5 on 2026-11-11 with Opus row L-R5.

what_went_wrong: No FTC press-release link (no internet)
rationale: Haiku could not open or verify a web address. The case is identified by name, court, year and amount, without a docket number. Haiku did write three bare agency web addresses from memory, which weakens the excuse slightly.

what_went_wrong: COPPA remedies: penalties noted but not court orders (expert memo has neither)
rationale: Haiku says enforcement can bring 'penalties paid to the government' and calls the 2019 case a consent judgment, but does not present court orders as a remedy. The expert's memo mentions only penalties (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: Amendments need both signatures; waivers need only the waiving party's signature. The expert's clause is built the same way
rationale: Section 13.6: amendments 'only by a written instrument signed by the Company and the Investor'; a waiver must be 'signed by the Party against which the waiver is asserted'. The item as written wants waivers signed by both. The expert's clause lets a term be waived 'in writing ... by the Party that is entitled to the benefit', so the expert does not meet it either.

what_went_wrong: Pre-emptive right includes an over-allotment up to the whole issuance
rationale: Section 7.3 lets the Investor buy New Securities beyond his Pro Rata Share, 'up to the total number of New Securities'. Not capped, so not met. It favours the client and the base right is pro rata as the task asked; classed like Opus's O2-L-22, though Haiku's version is unbracketed and wider.

what_went_wrong: No in-app or in-vehicle advertising lever
basis: fresh (same reasoning as H-F-15 and F-K2)
rationale: The task never mentions advertising; the deck proposes other levers (corporate accounts, a verified-driver tier, EV leases). Human ruling on F-K2 applies by the same reasoning.

what_went_wrong: Airport demand is addressed with fixed fares and a multilingual app, not a partnership with airport taxi companies or a similar channel
rationale: Segment 2 targets airport and inbound riders with 'fixed airport fares', a three-language UI and card payment; partnerships in the deck are with corporate fleets and lessors for supply. The task does not mention airports; an airport-fleet partnership is one tactic among several, as with advertising (F-K2) and regulator collaboration (S-F-12).

what_went_wrong: Driver experience is addressed through pay, shifts and coaching, not through a driver-app improvement
rationale: The deck offers an earnings floor, a published commission schedule, night-only shift packages and scorecards with coaching, but no change to the driver interface. The task names Korean user experience without singling out the driver app. Close to a minor real failure.

what_went_wrong: No s3937 question covers court relief; the workbook says s3937(c) is not tested
rationale: Instructions & Key C32 lists s3937(c) as not tested, and no question row mentions a court order. The expert's questions do not mention court relief either (decision rule 4).
